title: Decision: object-history arguments without the URI in using (handler-only or dispatcher-wide)
description:
Design: docs/design/object-history.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: D2. Crates: none (outcome may add a jmap-server follow-up). Size: S.

Context: docs/design/object-history.md §5 'Foo/get' and 'Foo/query', §12 Q1; docs/design/DECISIONS.md decision 2 (the conditional precedent).

H3 implements the interim rule. The _with_history handlers reject the following with invalidArguments when urn:ietf:params:jmap:object-history is not in using, and ignore the other history arguments:
- includeReplaced: true or includeDestroyed: true
- onlyDestroyed: true
- a non-null restore

Plain handlers keep ignoring these arguments. So a deployment without history silently returns live data for includeDestroyed:true and silently drops a restore write.

Question for Mark: extend the rejection to one dispatcher check on */get, */query and */set on every deployment, as decision 2 does for conditional? Recommended: yes.

Acceptance: the answer is recorded in docs/design/DECISIONS.md and note §12 Q1 is updated. If the answer is dispatcher-wide, file one S follow-up bead in jmap-server (it depends on H3) for the check and its dispatcher tests.
